scope: Historical anchors and contemporary evidence; precise gameplay probabilities and tuning are separately identified.

sources.observations: Outfit list pp.258-263; 200 lb flour, 30 pilot bread, 75 bacon, 10 rice, 25 sugar per adult, plus unweighed/other supplies. Hall/Boise emergency flour $20/100 lb. pp.289-291 reproduces a report of 200 lb pack horses on regional journeys with rest.
sources.limits: Not an 1848 Independence receipt or a universal carrying maximum; successful exceptional regional travel is not a family default. Mission resupply in the earlier account is not promised in the 1848 setting.

sources.observations: Chapters III-IV: ordinary walking marches with good grass/water and proper management need not reduce animal condition; long mule journeys recommended 125 lb. Region, grazing time, pace and overload matter. Notes winter differences between dry cured grass in Utah/New Mexico and the Missouri country.
sources.limits: Qualitative advice, not a daily wear equation. 125 lb is prudent advice, not a species maximum. No adoption of obsolete medical recipes or prejudiced character judgments.

sources.observations: Typical 2500 lb supply guideline; travelers commonly walked beside the wagon; broad four-six month and 10-15 miles/day context.
sources.limits: Interpretive summary spanning 1840s-1860s, not a precise 1848 itinerary, effective moving-day-only speed or numeric mortality target.

sources.observations: Timing departure for spring grass and clearing passes; avoid winter in the western mountains; opportunities differ across the route.
sources.limits: No reconstructed 1848 daily weather series or measured animal encounter odds.

sources.date: 115 deer measured during 2017 Ohio deer gun season
sources.observations: Mean 52.19 lb boneless venison from 107.56 lb field-dressed white-tailed deer; 48.52% yield. Sex/age mix and processing vary.
sources.limits: Modern Ohio white-tailed sample, not 1848 mule deer or guaranteed yield from every hit. Supports plausibility of current 42-85 usable lb, not exact species-wide bounds.

sources.date: NDSU publication FN124 reviewed May 2019, hosted by UC ANR
sources.observations: Venison is relatively lean; prompt cooling, clean handling and ambient heat affect spoilage. Nutrition table distinguishes water, fat, protein and energy.
sources.limits: Modern food-safety guidance is not an endorsement of unrefrigerated trail storage. Current fixed two-day raw meat life and 21/30-day dried life are authored abstractions, not safety instructions.

sources.date: Current cooperative extension guidance, checked October 24, 2026
sources.observations: Horses require substantial dry-matter forage; good managed pasture can meet maintenance needs for many healthy pleasure horses.
sources.limits: Managed pasture/light work is not an expedition under heavy loads. Body condition is simplified; game does not track actual hay, calories or grazing hours.

sources.date: Current NIH ODS professional fact sheet checked October 24, 2026
sources.observations: Scurvy follows sustained vitamin C deficiency, with symptoms potentially appearing within a month; stored body reserves and actual intake matter.
sources.limits: No direct conversion from a basket's pounds to vitamin dose; game half-pound produce meal and dried retention are tuning, not clinical thresholds.

sources.observations: Measured foraging travel depends on tasks, local ecology and route geometry; daily search distance differs from point-to-point migration.
sources.limits: Cannot transfer a group mean to maximum marching speed, random emigrant expertise or ethnicity/sex modifiers. Real subsistence includes knowledge, sharing and more foods than game greens.

sources.observations: Subsistence can yield high returns with substantial effort, technology, cooperation and variable outcomes.
sources.limits: Does not justify guaranteed daily success or complete nutrition from lean meat or greens alone.

sources.observations: Added backpack load increases work and metabolic cost.
sources.limits: Fixed treadmill conditions do not establish the game's linear health-to-capacity rule, broken-leg binary exclusion or fixed personal gear mass.

sources.date: 1850 federal census compendium reporting 1848 inquiry and 1850 local wages
sources.observations: Printed pp.164-165 distinguish boarded field labor and skilled/unboarded wages. Detailed prior inspection and calculations are in HISTORICAL_ECONOMY.md.
sources.limits: Not a surveyed emigrant-companion contract market; premiums for traits and profession starting cash remain authored. Previously inspected scan, not newly remeasured in this pass.

sources.observations: Disease, accidents, drowning and weather dominate the account; accidental shootings common, murder comparatively rare. It gives broad multi-decade mortality estimates.
sources.limits: Not a one-year Oregon-only control sample. Do not force every five-person game's death or win frequency to this aggregate, and do not use classic encounter frequencies as historical measurements.

sources.observations: Carry caps and hunting encounters are game design decisions; regional variety and player aiming matter.
sources.limits: Previously inspected in research/ECONOMY_PRESERVATION_SOURCES.json. 1978 BASIC quantities, 1985 budgets and 1993 GUI are reference behavior, not a common real-world unit system or historical price list.
